question: Should Microsoft Teams permanently adopt the shared channel multi-account model—`accounts`, `defaultAccount`, inherited root settings, account-scoped credentials and state—while retaining legacy root credentials as the default account?
rationale: The implementation is credible, but this choice creates long-lived configuration, setup, credential, and persisted-state compatibility obligations that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Sponsor the contract
options.body: Approve the proposed Teams account model, then reopen or refresh the PR and require current-main upgrade and live multi-bot validation before landing.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and request a smaller design that reduces inheritance, setup rewriting, or persisted-state surface before accepting implementation.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep Teams single-account in one gateway and document separate gateway instances as the supported identity-isolation model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the contract
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed Teams account model, then reopen or refresh the PR and require current-main upgrade and live multi-bot validation before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a channel-wide public configuration and compatibility choice, and available discussion/history most strongly routes that decision here.
